commitResults.messageTitle: Specify level of experience in programming and IDE in AGENTS.md
Add items to memory and display items in memory
Add todo, deadline and event. Add error messages
Update deadline and event to use LocalDateTime
Add JUnit tests for Parser and Storage
Add assertions to classes related to task
commitResults.messageBody:
Assertions are missing from classes which create and update tasks.

Assertions can document important assumptions when creating and
updating tasks.

Let's add assertions to Deadline, Event, Task, TaskList and Parser.

This will ensure,
* Deadline and Event are created with valid properties
* Index which refers to a task in the list is valid

Task-addition and task-deletion replies each build the same task and
task-count message structure.

Maintaining that structure in two places risks inconsistent responses
when its formatting changes.

Centralize the shared response structure in Response while preserving
the command-specific opening messages.

Task-record parsing relies on raw field indexes and literal codes for
the separator, task type, completion status, and date-time fields.

Those unnamed values make the persistence format difficult to read and
increase the risk of using the wrong field when the format changes.

Name the task-file format elements in Storage while preserving the
existing serialized format and parsing behaviour.

Task type codes are duplicated across each task subclass and Storage. 
The duplicated definitions make the task-file format harder to 
understand and risk serialization and parsing diverging.

Represent the finite set of task types with TaskType and give that type 
ownership of the persistent code. This keeps the existing task-file 
format unchanged while making the shared format contract explicit.

Mark, unmark, and delete each retrieve a task directly from the 
internal list. Repeating that access detail distracts from the 
operation each method performs.

Centralize task retrieval behind a named helper so the public methods 
describe their task-state or list-changing action. This preserves their 
existing index handling and behaviour.

Response methods repeatedly construct a list of lines and join it with 
line breaks. The repeated formatting obscures the message content each 
method is responsible for.

Centralize line joining in Response so each method only specifies its 
message lines. This retains all existing response text and layout while 
reducing duplicated formatting logic.

Task supplies shared state and behaviour for Todo, Deadline, and Event, 
but it does not represent a complete task kind by itself.

Leaving Task concrete permits creating a task without a meaningful kind 
or task-specific data.

Declare Task abstract to make its role explicit and prevent incomplete 
task instances while preserving the existing subclass API.

readTasks initializes the file contents as an empty string before 
attempting to read. If reading fails, execution continues as though the 
storage file were empty.

That fallback hides the failure path and makes the variable serve two 
unrelated purposes.

Return after reporting a read error so that the successful path only 
processes data actually read from storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Separate routing from error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
parse both selects a command handler and converts command exceptions 
into user-facing responses. Mixing those concerns makes the method 
harder to read and obscures its error-handling policy.

Extract command routing into a dedicated helper. The public method now 
clearly expresses that it returns either a command result or the 
corresponding error response, without changing command behaviour.

getArgument builds command arguments one character at a time even 
though an argument is a contiguous substring between a flag and the 
next slash.

The loop hides that simple rule and adds low-level control flow to a 
method whose purpose is parsing command segments.

Use substring boundaries to state the extraction rule directly while 
preserving missing-argument validation and command syntax.

Task subclasses repeat responsibility for adding their type prefix to
user-facing output, even though Task already owns the task type.

Let Task render its own type prefix and derive that prefix from
TaskType's file code. Todo can now inherit the base representation,
while Deadline and Event only append their date details.
